tasks.title: Evaluation of Phytoremediation Efficiency in Heavy Metal Wastewater Processing
tasks.prompt: To what extent does the utilization of Eichhornia crassipes in industrial wastewater treatment protocols effectively mitigate heavy metal toxicity without compromising systemic ecological stability?

stimulus.title: Trial Log 04B: Aquatic Phytoremediation Protocol & Anomaly Observations
stimulus.content: Continuous-flow bioreactor testing evaluated Eichhornia crassipes bioaccumulation of Lead (Pb2+) over 14 days under controlled environmental parameters (pH 6.5, 22°C). Root necrosis and organic exudate leakage were registered during the final phase.
keyPoints: Lead ion concentration declined by 88.4% within the first 8 days of exposure.
Cellular uptake rates dropped from 4.2 mg/g/day (Days 1-5) to 0.3 mg/g/day (Days 10-14).
Day 10 root saturation triggered a 14% rebound in Dissolved Organic Carbon (DOC) due to biological tissue decay.
stimulus.notes: Regulatory discharge threshold for Pb2+ is 0.05 mg/L; root tissue saturation threshold occurs at 45 mg Pb2+/g dry biomass.

stimulus.content: Engineering specifications targeting a lightweight wearable upper-limb support for geriatric users with rheumatoid arthritis. Primary functional requirement demands 25Nm lifting assistance while remaining under 1.2 kg total mass.

stimulus.notes: ISO 9241-210 human-centered design compliance requires continuous comfortable wear duration of at least 60 minutes.
